summary: Fixed-size job table (submit / run / cancel / collect) with payloads in a caller-provided byte array. In v1 js_cancel frees a slot even while its callback is executing, so a re-entrant or interrupt-level cancel races the runner: the slot can be reused by a new submit and then overwritten by the old run (race condition, CWE-362); v2 locks the slot for the duration of the callback and defers a cancel that arrives meanwhile; v3 is a behaviour-preserving refactor of v2.

pairs.intent: CWE-362 fix: js_run sets JS_FLAG_LOCKED around the callback and honours a pending JS_FLAG_CANCEL afterwards; js_cancel refuses to free a locked slot (returns JS_ERR_BUSY and records the request) using the new js_is_locked predicate; the unconditional js_force_free helper is removed.

truth.label: changed
truth.notes: CWE-362: no lock around the callback; after it returned the runner wrote result and JS_DONE into a slot that a concurrent cancel/submit might already have recycled. v2 locks the slot and releases it itself if a cancel was requested.

truth.label: changed
truth.notes: CWE-362: freed a RUNNING slot immediately; v2 checks the lock flag first and defers the cancel to the runner (JS_ERR_BUSY).
